svg.text: Where the agent information lives, and how it reaches the marketplace
Data Hub (BigQuery) is the system of record. The application holds no durable copy of the catalogue.
Three, and only three, ways a row enters or changes in the catalogue. Every one of them lands in the same table and leaves the same audit record.

Latest action per voter wins, at read
The application never reads a row, changes it and writes it back. A vote is an event,
and the count is a view over those events. Ten Cloud Run instances can therefore
accept votes at the same moment without a lock and without losing one. This is also
why the vote count survived moving off the single-instance pilot.
Rejected: Firestore for hot state with BigQuery as an analytics sink. It performs better on paper, but it splits the system of record across two stores with two
access models, two retention mechanisms and two lineage stories to explain. At this data volume the single governed store wins. If read latency ever becomes the
constraint, the answer is a cache in front of BigQuery, not a second source of truth.
Why BigQuery is fast enough to serve a UI
Catalogue reads are a few hundred rows and are cached for 300 seconds, so a BigQuery round trip happens at most twelve times an hour per instance. Cost is
immaterial and p95 page render stays under the 1.5 second budget. BI Engine is available if the budget tightens.
